(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAMACHANDRA D. HUDDAR)

The appellant-Insurance Company has preferred this appeal challenging the quantum of compensation awarded to the claimants vide common judgment dated 25.10.2023 in MVC No.1192 and 1193/2022 on the file of II Addl. Senior Civil Judge & Member, MACT-7, Vijayapura, awarding compensation in so far as claimants in MVC No.1192/2022 at Rs. 30,36,268/- under all relevant heads together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Parties to this appeal are referred to as per their rank before the trial Court.
3.

It is the case of claimants before the Tribunal that, one Karthik Gayakwad died on account of injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.6.2022 at about 8.30 p.m. near Dosti Dhaba on Solapur - Pandarapur road at Pandarpur when he was on the extreme end of the road.

It is stated that, at that time, NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB because of rash and negligent driving of the tanker bearing Reg. No.MH-46-F-3780 by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against deceased and he died.

It is stated that, deceased was getting substantial income towards maintenance of the family and because of untimely death of the deceased, now the claimants are suffering lot both financially and mentally.
Thus, claimants filed claim petition before the Tribunal claming compensation.
4. Before the Tribunal, both the respondents appeared and contested the petition by filing detailed written statements.
Respondent No.1 has denied the nature of the accident, claim of the petitioners so also death of Karthik in the said accident, and income earned by the deceased.
So far as respondent No.2 Insurance Company is concerned, he has denied all the averments in the petition.
It is contended that, there is no nexus between the alleged accident and the insured vehicle.
The said vehicle has been falsely implicated by the police.
There was delay in filing the complaint.
As there is violation of the policy conditions by respondent No.1, Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Based upon the rival contentions between both the parties, the Tribunal framed relevant issues.
To prove the claim of the claimants, PW.2 Sunitha Gayakwad the claimant No.2 being wife of deceased Karthik entered the witness box.
Several documents were marked as per Exs.P.1 to P.8 on behalf of these claimants.
The respondents have not lead any oral evidence whereas respondent No.2 has produced the copy of the Insurance Policy which is marked as Ex.R1 with consent.

6. On considering the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the said accident has taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the Tanker by its driver.

It is also held NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB that the claimants are entitled for the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads of compensation Amount  No.
 1 Loss of dependency Rs.29,51,268/-
2 Loss
of spousal consortium

7.

So far as liability is concerned, as the Insurance Policy was in force as on the date of the accident pertaining to the offending vehicle, it is proved by the claimants that there was no violation of policy terms and conditions, the Tribunal held that both respondents are liable to pay the compensation,
however, as issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident is not denied by the respondent no.2, it directed the Insurance Company to indemnify the compensation.

This is how,
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB now the Insurance Company is before this Court challenging the said compensation awarded in this case, challenging fastening of liability on it and on quantum.

8. The learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company submits that the very calculation of the income of the deceased at the time of the accident in question is not proper on the part of the Tribunal.

Learned counsel Smt. Preethi Patil submits that the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- which according to the her is not based on the Circular issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The income ought to have been calculated at Rs.14,750/-.
The Insurance Company is disputing award of compensation under conventional heads also.

She submits that because of the wrong calculation made by the Tribunal, the compensation awarded to the claimants is on higher side and it has to be reduced by taking the income of the deceased at Rs.14,750/- as the accident has taken place in the year 2022.

As regards this submission, the learned counsel for the claimants submits that, though the Tribunal has committed wrong in calculating the income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- but, the Tribunal has not awarded towards loss of consortium to other dependents so also there must be 10%
hike in the said amount.
It is not properly calculated as there are three claimants, each of the claimants are entitled for consortium of Rs. 40,000/- each with 10% hike.
Therefore, he submits that the other claimants are also entitled for enhanced compensation other than claimant No.2.
He admits that no separate appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the question of not awarding the consortium.
10. Further, the learned counsel for the appellant Smt. Preethi Patil submits that without preferring a separate appeal, now the claimants cannot seek any enhancement of compensation.
She submits that such a submission cannot be accepted.

NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB The Manager vs Laxmibai on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58508851/
4 11.
So far as income of the deceased is concerned, as rightly submitted by both the side, the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/-.
As per the Circular issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the income of the deceased ought to have been reckoned at Rs.14,750/-.

In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, as the deceased was aged within 40 years at the time of accident, 40% is to be added towards his future prospects which comes to Rs.5,900/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the total income of the deceased would be Rs.14,750/- + Rs.5,900/- =
Rs.20,650/-.

Out of this, as the claimants were the dependents and deceased died leaving behind them, 1/3rd of total income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased and remainder has to be multiplied.
As the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of his death, the proper multiplier that is applicable is '17' that means Rs.20,650x2/3x12x17= Rs.28,08,400/-.

So far as other - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB heads are concerned, the Tribunal has awarded compensation towards consortium to claimant No.2 at Rs.40,000/- so also towards love and affection, funeral expenses and loss of estate at Rs.15,000/- each.
In our opinion, whatever the compensation so awarded under these heads is just and proper.
12. It is argued by the counsel for the claimants that the loss of consortium is to be awarded to the claimant Nos.1 and 3.

As no separate appeal is preferred by the claimant however, by exercising power under Section 41, Rule 33 of CPC, this Court can grant relief to the claimants as the Motor Vehicle Act is a social/benevolent legislation.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation to claimant No.2 being wife towards loss of consortium, but, has not awarded consortium to claimant Nos.2 and 3 being the children of deceased.
Hence, compensation towards loss of consortium is to be awarded to these claimants also.
Since the accident is of the year 2022, 10% enhancement is required to be made to the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB loss of consortium.
Thus, in addition to the compensation awarded to Claimant NO.1 at Rs.40,000/-, Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to claimant Nos. 2 and 3 towards `loss of consortium' with 10% hike.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000 x 3 = 1,20,000/- + 10%
it would be Rs.1,32,000/- towards loss of consortium.

Thus, claimants are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Compensation  No. Awarded Rs.
1.
Loss of dependency 28,08,400-00 2. Funeral expenses and 15,000-00  obsequies ceremonies 3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 4. Loss of consortium 1,32,000-00 5. Loss of love and affection 15,000-00

awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Thus, the appellant-Insurance Company succeeds in part..
Claimants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.29,85,400/- thereby reducing the compensation amount by Rs.50,868/-.
Though the Tribunal has awarded interest at 6% on whole amount but, the claimants are not entitled for interest on future prospects.

Therefore,
the Tribunal has to calculate the interest on future prospects and on that future prospects, the claimants shall not claim any interest.

14. Resultantly, we pass the following :-
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in-part.
(ii) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.29,85,400/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation excluding the interest for future prospects.
(iii) There shall be modified award in the above terms.
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6993-DB (iv) The amount deposited by the appellant before this Court if any, be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
(v) Send back the trial court records along with a copy of this judgment.
